Park Geun-hye: President of South Korea from 2013 to 2017. Park previously served as the acting first lady of South Korea under her father's presidency from 1974 until her father's assassination in 1979.
Possibly descended from Aegean migrants who settled Canaan's southern coast around 1175 BC, this Iron Age people organized their territory into a confederation of city-states — who were they?
Philistines: Ancient people who inhabited Canaan's southern coast.
The Zabur, revealed to David before the Quran alongside the Torah and Gospel, is Muslim tradition's term for what collection of David's sacred songs?
Psalms in Islam: Holy book of the prophet Dawud.
This ten-headed demon king of Lanka abducted the hero's wife in an ancient Hindu epic and is now burned in effigy every year during a festival marking his defeat — who is he?
Ravana: Primary antagonist in the Hindu epic Ramayana.
Nicknamed 'Fighting Bob,' this Wisconsin progressive served as governor and senator before running for president in 1924 on a party he made himself — who is it?
Robert M. La Follette: American lawyer and politician (1855–1925)
Nicknamed Iran's 'hanging judge,' this cleric headed the country's revolutionary court from 1979 to 1981 and ordered the destruction of a former shah's mausoleum — who was he?
Sadegh Khalkhali: Iranian cleric and politician (1926–2003)
This Roman general's victory over Hannibal at the Battle of Zama in 202 BC earned him an honorific epithet referencing the continent he conquered — who was he?
Scipio Africanus: Roman general and politician (236/235 – c. 183 BC)
Daughter of Bangladesh's first president, she became the country's longest-serving prime minister and one of the world's longest-serving female heads of government — who is she?
Sheikh Hasina: Prime Minister of Bangladesh (1996–2001; 2009–2024)
Established as a client state of Nazi Germany in March 1939, this Central European nation's army also joined the invasion of Poland that year — which state, whose capital was Bratislava?
Slovak Republic (1939–1945): Client state of Nazi Germany. The Slovak part of Czechoslovakia declared independence with German support one day before the German occupation of Bohemia and Moravia.
Established by Seljuk Turks after their victory over Byzantine forces at Manzikert in 1071, this Turco-Persian state is considered the beginning of Turkish history in Anatolia. What was it?
Sultanate of Rum: Turkish state in central Anatolia from 1077 to 1308.
This biblical figure, son of Nahor, is best known as the father of the patriarch Abraham in the Book of Genesis — who is he?
Terah: Figure in the Hebrew Bible; son of Nahor.
The eighth shogun of his family's shogunate, ruling from 1716 to 1745, this samurai is remembered for repealing Japan's ban on Western literature — who was he?
Tokugawa Yoshimune: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1716 to 1745.
As third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, this son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad ordered the standardized compilation of the Quran still used today — who was he?
Credited with coining the phrase 'sovereign democracy' while shaping Kremlin strategy for over a decade, this close Putin aide earned the nickname 'grey cardinal' — who is he?
As chief of the OKW, this German field marshal signed the criminal orders that fed countless war crimes — and was so deferential to Hitler that colleagues reviled him. Who was he?
Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams to promote 'muscular Christianity,' this youth organization now serves over 64 million people worldwide?
YMCA: Worldwide youth organization. YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.
Emerging in late-19th-century Europe in reaction to antisemitism and led by Theodor Herzl, this nationalist movement sought a Jewish homeland in Palestine — what is it?
Zionism: Jewish nationalist movement. The arrival of Zionist settlers in Palestine during this period is widely seen as marking the start of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
Who among these was born first?
George Grove (born 1820) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four. Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
Which one below was born first?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four. Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Annie S. D. Maunder is an astronomer. As sole author, she also devised with her husband, Edward Walter Maunder, the butterfly diagram for sunspots.
Pick the mathematician from these four.

William James Sidis is a mathematician. Born to Boris Sidis, a prominent psychiatrist, and Sarah Mandelbaum Sidis, a physician, Sidis demonstrated extraordinary intellectual capabilities from infancy.
What is the atomic number of Tellurium?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
What is the atomic number of Manganese?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
In what year was David Attenborough born?
David Attenborough: Sir David Frederick Attenborough ( AT-ən-bər-ə; born 8 May 1926) is an English broadcaster, natural historian, and writer.
In what year was Eratosthenes born?
Eratosthenes eventually became the chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.
In what year was Michael Faraday born?
Michael Faraday: Although Faraday received little formal education, as a self-made man, he was one of the most influential scientists in history.
In what year did Carlo Acutis die?
Carlo Acutis: Acutis was canonised on 7 September 2025, alongside Pier Giorgio Frassati.
In what year did Srinivasa Ramanujan die?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Uncertainty principle discovered?
Uncertainty principle: The uncertainty principle, also known as Heisenberg's indeterminacy principle, is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics.

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Approximately 60 countries across four continents have flown the MiG-21, and it still serves many nations seven decades after its maiden flight.
Zinc: Pfizer. Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In which country is Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker?
Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker: United States. It has a narrower fuselage and is shorter than the 707.
Who is credited with discovering Roentgenium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Roentgenium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Roentgenium (German: [ʁœntˈɡeːni̯ʊm]) is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
Who is credited with discovering 4 Vesta?
4 Vesta: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Vesta (minor-planet designation: 4 Vesta) is one of the largest objects in the asteroid belt, with a mean diameter of 525 kilometres (326 mi).
Who is credited with discovering Lysosome?
Lysosome: Christian de Duve. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.
People with this anxiety disorder dread places they feel they can't escape — crowds, queues, public transit — and in severe cases may become unable to leave home at all. What is it?
Agoraphobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by symptoms of anxiety in situations where the person perceives their environment to be unsafe with no way to escape.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and almost always monogamous breeders, which bird family unites ducks, geese, and swans under one scientific name?
Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.
Native to Europe but introduced to North America, this orb-weaver spider species is known by several common names, one of them shared confusingly with a different species — which species?
Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.

With the symbol Ba and atomic number 56, this soft, silvery alkaline earth metal is so reactive it's never found free in nature, and takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'heavy' — name this element?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
This colourless industrial compound, easily dissolved in organic solvents but not water, is the key ingredient in most polycarbonate plastics — which chemical?
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical compound primarily used in the manufacturing of various plastics.
Formed naturally through evaporation of saline water or generated by salt mining, which concentrated saltwater solution helps de-ice roads and preserve pickled foods?
Brine (or briny water) is a high-concentration solution of salt (typically sodium chloride or calcium chloride) in water.
Chili peppers likely make this hydrophobic compound to deter hungry mammals and fungi — yet it's exactly what gives them their burning, pungent heat. What is it?
Capsaicin (8-methyl-N-vanillyl-6-nonenamide) (commonly) is a toxin that is the main active component of chili peppers and gives them their distinct pungent, "spicy" or "hot" taste.
Domesticated from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia about 8,000 years ago, this social bird now numbers over 26.5 billion worldwide — what is it?
Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Whose larvae track down plant roots to eat by sensing both leaf-released volatiles and carbon dioxide, in a European scarab species also known as the Maybeetle?
Cockchafer (Melolontha melolontha), also colloquially known as the Maybug, Maybeetle, or doodlebug, is a species of scarab beetle belonging to the genus Melolontha.
In this satirical action comedy, a group of self-absorbed actors filming a war movie are dropped in the jungle by their fed-up director and must rely on real survival skills. What film is it?
Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
This genus of roughly 340 species includes the carnation and the sweet william, and is nicknamed 'pink' — which genus?

Dianthus (dy-) is a genus of about 340 species of flowering plants in the family Caryophyllaceae, native mainly to Europe and Asia, with a few species in northern and southern Africa, and one species (D. repens) in arctic North America.
Born in Dublin in 1869 into an old Anglo-Irish scientific family, she's considered the very first woman to work as a medical physicist — who was she?
Edith Anne Stoney (6 January 1869 - 25 June 1938) was an Irish physicist.
This taxonomic family groups hedgehogs of Eurasia and Africa together with the furrier moonrats of Southeast Asia, and takes its name from the Latin for 'hedgehog' — what family is it?
Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.

Native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, this fig species carries deep religious significance across four faiths that originated there, including reverence from Hindu and Jain ascetics — what species is it?
Ficus religiosa is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.

This inflammation of the stomach lining is commonly caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, and can lead to complications like ulcers or, in its autoimmune form, pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis is the inflammation of the lining of the stomach. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.

Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, these ground-dwelling herbivorous insects use powerful hind legs to leap away from danger and hatch as nymphs that molt five times — what's the insect?
Grasshopper are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.
This naturally occurring molecule and medication is a powerful blood anticoagulant used to treat heart attacks and prevent clotting in dialysis machines and test tubes — what is it?
Heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
This endocrine condition floods the body with thyroid hormone, causing a racing heart, heat intolerance, tremor, and weight loss — and a rare 'storm' can be deadly; what is it?
Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.
This Confederate veteran and pharmacist sold the rights to his 1886 beverage recipe to Asa Griggs Candler for about $2,300 shortly before he died — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton (July 8, 1831 - August 16, 1888) was an American pharmacist, chemist, and Confederate States Army officer who is best known as the inventor of Coca-Cola.
Endemic to New Zealand, this large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot has owl-like forward-facing eyes and holds the title of the world's only flightless parrot — what bird is it?
Kākāpō (Mori:; pl.: kkp; Strigops habroptilus), sometimes known as the owl-parrot, is a species of large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot of the superfamily Strigopoidea.
Born in 1880, this Australian therapist and part-time stage actor is remembered for coaching a stammering British monarch — who is he?
Lionel Logue (26 February 1880 - 12 April 1953) was an Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor who helped King George VI manage his stammer.

An engineer and teacher from a poor family who once served as mayor of Tehran, this politician became Iran's sixth president in 2005 and was a fierce proponent of the country's nuclear program — who is he?
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (n Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.
First made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, this synthetic element 101 is named for the father of the periodic table — what is it?
Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.
This SI base unit for amount of substance, symbol mol, is defined so that one unit contains exactly 6.02214076×10²³ elementary entities — what is it called?
Mole (unit) (symbol mol) is a unit of measurement, the base unit in the International System of Units (SI) for amount of substance.

Which form of alternative medicine, rooted in vitalism and folk healing rather than evidence, gathers 'natural' and 'self-healing' practices ranging from discredited homeopathy to accepted psychotherapy?
Naturopathy is a form of alternative medicine. The ethics of naturopathy have been called into question by medical professionals and its practice has been characterized as quackery.

Classified using a measurement of weight divided by the square of height, this medical condition is diagnosed when that figure exceeds 30 and is linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes — what is it?
Obesity is a medical condition, considered a disease by multiple organizations, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that it can have negative effects on health.

This genus of 70 to 100 frost-tolerant annual, biennial, and perennial species native to temperate Eurasia, Africa, and North America is the type genus of its flowering plant family — what's the genus?
Papaver is a genus of 70-100 species of frost-tolerant annuals, biennials, and perennials native to temperate and cold regions of Eurasia, Africa and North America.
A self-described socialist active in Finland's Pirate Party, this entrepreneur co-founded a famous file-sharing search engine and later started the privacy service Njalla — who is he?
Peter Sunde (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Derived enzymatically from a fatty acid found in nearly every tissue of the body, this class of lipid compounds produces diverse hormone-like effects despite not being true hormones — what are they called?
Prostaglandin (PG) are a group of physiologically active lipid compounds that have diverse hormone-like effects in animals.
Distinguished from its smaller relative the crow mainly by size, this large-bodied passerine bird genus includes the common and thick-billed species, the biggest passerines alive — what bird is it?
Raven is any of several large-bodied passerine bird species in the genus Corvus.
Created by Yukihiro 'Matz' Matsumoto in 1990s Japan, this dynamically typed programming language treats absolutely everything — even primitive data types — as an object — what's the language?
Ruby (programming language) is a general-purpose programming language designed with an emphasis on programming productivity and simplicity.
Which chemical element, symbol Se, was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named for the moon, in a nod to its chemical similarity to tellurium, named for the Earth?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
With the formula CH3COONa, this colorless, moisture-absorbing salt of acetic acid is deliquescent, meaning it can even dissolve in the water it pulls from the air — which compound?
Sodium acetate is a chemical compound with formula CH3COONa, also abbreviated NaOAc.
This muscular, hollow organ in the upper digestive tract handles the gastric phase of digestion, and gives us the medical prefix 'gastric' from its Ancient Greek name — name the organ?
Stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the upper gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.

This chalcogen element, chemically similar to selenium and sulfur, is far more abundant in the universe than on Earth because its hydride escaped into space during our planet's formation — which element?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial flowering plant is the type species of its genus and a member of the honeysuckle family — which herb?
Valerian (herb) (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
A physician, painter, and inventor, this man designed the United States Capitol and served as both the first Architect of the Capitol and the first head of the Patent Office — who was he?
William Thornton (May 20, 1759 - March 28, 1828) was an American physician, inventor, painter and architect who designed the United States Capitol.
This American psychologist devised a pyramid-shaped theory of human needs culminating in self-actualization, and was later ranked the 10th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century — who is he?

First flown as a stretched derivative of a popular narrow-body jet family in 1994, this twin-engine airliner carries up to 239 passengers and later gained a fuel-efficient 'neo' version with new winglets — which aircraft?
Airbus A321: Airliner, stretched model of the A320 family.

The brightest star in the constellation Aquila and a vertex of the Summer Triangle, this nearby A-type star spins so fast — about 286 km/s at its equator — that it bulges noticeably. Which star is it?
Altair: Brightest star in the constellation Aquila. Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky.
Likened to a bubble or balloon, this outward bulge forms at a weak spot in a blood-vessel wall and grows ever more dangerous as it risks rupture — what is it?
Aneurysm: Bulge in the wall of a blood vessel. An aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
This genus of orb-weaving spiders, encompassing the European garden spider and the barn spider among its 500-plus species, was named by an 18th-century Swedish naturalist in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus: Genus of spiders. The genus was erected by Carl Alexander Clerck in 1757.
Found from the Labrador Sea to the Barents Sea and able to live up to 25 years, this widely eaten fish can occasionally top 180 centimeters and 50 kilograms — what species is it?
Atlantic cod: Species of fish. The Atlantic cod (pl.: cod; Gadus morhua) is a fish of the family Gadidae, widely consumed by humans.
Bred in Britain to hunt rabbits and hares, this scent hound's keen nose also makes it a popular detection dog for smuggled food at airports — which breed?
Beagle: Breed of small scent hound. The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
Prized for the rainbow, iridescent crust that forms when it oxidizes under heat, which brittle, silvery element is only 86 percent as dense as lead?
Bismuth: Chemical element with atomic number 83 (Bi)
This highly venomous snake in the Colubridae family, scientifically known as Dispholidus typus, is native to Sub-Saharan Africa — what is its common name?
Buried penis: Male congenital condition. A buried penis can lead to urinary difficulties, poor hygiene, infection, and inhibition of normal sexual function.
Its Latin name means 'horned goat,' and it's often pictured as a half-goat, half-fish sea creature — which is the smallest constellation of the zodiac?
Capricornus: Zodiac constellation in the southern hemisphere.

Nicknamed the 'solar' web for its sunburst of radiating nerve fibers, this abdominal structure sits behind the stomach and in front of the diaphragm's crura, near where several major arteries branch off the aorta — what is it?
Celiac plexus: Complex network of nerves located in the upper abdomen.
Discovered entirely by accident and marketed as Librium, this 1960-approved medication was the first benzodiazepine ever synthesized — what is it?
Chlordiazepoxide: Benzodiazepine medication. Chlordiazepoxide hydrochloride, sold under the brand name Librium, is a sedative and hypnotic medication of the benzodiazepine class.
This little Indo-Pacific reef fish, banded in white, shelters among stinging tentacles and repays the favor by fending off anemone-eaters and fanning its host clean. What fish is it?
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
The second jet fighter to enter RAF service and the first powered by a single jet engine, this twin-boom aircraft flew with the Halford Goblin turbojet — which aircraft?

De Havilland Vampire: Fighter aircraft; first single-engine jet in RAF service. The de Havilland DH100 Vampire is a British jet fighter developed and manufactured by the de Havilland Aircraft Company.

Previously known as multiple personality condition and popularized (inaccurately) by the case of 'Sybil,' this controversial mental health diagnosis is characterized by the presence of two or more distinct personality states known as 'alters' — which condition is this?
Dissociative identity disorder: Mental illness with multiple personality states.
Its leaves and flowers are covered in dense white hairs that shield it from Alpine cold and UV rays, making this daisy-family flower a symbol of mountaineering purity — what is it?
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This centuries-old number theory statement claims there are no positive whole-number solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n whenever the exponent exceeds two — what's it called?
Fermat's Last Theorem: 17th-century conjecture proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994.
Part of the rose family and prized for fruit that ranges from very sweet to notably tart, this genus's garden hybrid is an important commercial crop worldwide — which genus is it?
One of Maxwell's equations, this application of the divergence theorem connects electric charge distribution to the electric field it creates. Which one is it?
Gauss's law: Foundational law of electromagnetism relating electric field and charge distributions.
The simplest and only non-chiral of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids, this compound makes up about 35% of collagen's amino acid content — what is it?
Glycine: Amino acid. In the body, glycine plays several crucial roles.
Also nicknamed the millionfish, this livebearing freshwater fish is one of the world's most popular aquarium species — which fish?

This airway symptom — blood or blood-streaked mucus coughed up from the lungs or throat — turns dangerous mainly because of choking rather than blood loss once it passes 300 milliliters. What is it called?

The only birds whose first two neck vertebrae are fused together, these Old World birds have a long down-curved bill sometimes topped with a bony casque, and share an ecological niche with toucans in the Americas — which birds?
Hornbill: Family of birds. The family is omnivorous, feeding on fruit and small animals.
About the size of an almond in humans, this brain structure links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus: Area of the brain below the thalamus.
Symbol Fe, atomic number 26, it's the most common element on Earth by mass and forms much of the planet's core — yet smelting it needs furnaces 500°C hotter than copper does. Which metal?
Iron: Chemical element with atomic number 26 (Fe)
With Emmanuelle Charpentier, this Berkeley biochemist proposed in 2012 that CRISPR-Cas9 could edit genomes — work that won them the 2020 Nobel in Chemistry; who is she?
Jennifer Doudna: American biochemist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
Nicknamed the 'miracle leaf' and 'life plant,' this Madagascar-native succulent sprouts tiny new plantlets right along the edges of its leaves — which species?

Kalanchoe pinnata: Succulent plant native to Madagascar. Kalanchoe pinnata, commonly known as cathedral bells, air plant, life plant, miracle leaf, and love bush, is a succulent plant native to Madagascar.
Once a water retriever in Italy's Po Delta marshlands, this Italian dog breed later became prized for sniffing out truffles — which breed?
Lagotto Romagnolo: Italian breed of dog.
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?
This French chemist's discoveries in fermentation and vaccination gave us a heat-treatment process that now bears his name and rabies and anthrax vaccines — who was he?
Louis Pasteur: French chemist, pharmacist and microbiologist (1822–1895)
In larger organizations it stacks into a pyramid, with a board and CEO at the top setting strategy — the broad practice of administering a business or government. What is it?
Management: Coordinating the efforts of persons.
Home to the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and central chest lymph nodes, this compartment of the thoracic cavity sits between the lungs — what's it called?
Mediastinum: Central part of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum (from Medieval Latin: mediastinus, lit. 'midway';pl.: mediastina) is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.
This development economist shared the 2019 Nobel with Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty — who is he?
Michael Kremer: American economist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Most often triggered by a viral infection and capable of progressing to heart failure or cardiac arrest, which condition involves inflammation of the heart muscle itself?

Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
This Danish physicist won the 1922 Nobel Prize for a model of the atom in which electrons leap between discrete, stable orbits around the nucleus — who is he?

Symbolized by the Greek letter omega, this SI unit of electrical resistance was named after a 19th-century German physicist and, since 2019, is defined as an exact value based on fundamental constants — what unit is it?
Ohm: SI derived unit of electrical resistance. The ohm (symbol: Ω, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compound pairs oxygen with another element — the same chemistry behind the thin protective layer on aluminium foil — what is it called?
Oxide: Compounds containing an oxygen atom.
Born in the Soviet Union, this entrepreneur co-founded a social network in 2006 before developing a messaging app now headquartered in Dubai — who is he?

Approved for medical use in the US back in 1959 and sold under the brand name Adipex-P, this appetite-suppressing stimulant is a substituted amphetamine used alongside diet and exercise to treat obesity — what is it?
Its name comes from the Spanish for 'little silver,' yet this dense, stubbornly unreactive metal — element 78 — is so scarce only a few hundred tonnes are mined a year. Which one?
Platinum: Chemical element with atomic number 78 (Pt)

Arising over 60 million years ago from small tree-dwellers, this order favored big brains, binocular color vision and opposable thumbs to grasp among the branches — and it includes lemurs and apes — what is it?
Primate: Order of mammals. New primate species continue to be discovered: over 25 species were described in the 2000s, 36 in the 2010s, and six in the 2020s.

Known in France as the Patou and in the US by another name, this French livestock guardian breed hails from a range straddling France and Spain, protecting flocks from wolves and bears. What breed is it?
Pyrenean Mountain Dog: French breed of dog. The Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Chien de Montagne des Pyrénées) is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.
From a startled jump to a cat automatically reorienting itself mid-fall, this involuntary, split-second reaction runs through the nervous system without needing conscious thought — what's it called?
Reflex: Automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus.
Usually hidden underground, this plant organ anchors it in place while drawing in water and nutrients — what is it?
Root: Basal organ of a vascular plant.

With ears set low to detect prey moving underground and furry paw soles that insulate against scorching ground, this small desert feline was first described in the Algerian Sahara in 1858 — which animal?
Sand cat: Small wild cat species (Felis margarita)

Nicknamed the 'last Soviet citizen' for being aboard Mir when the USSR dissolved, this cosmonaut flew six missions and helped connect the first Russian and American modules of a space station — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev: Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (born 1958)

Thanks to extra joints in its skull, this legless, scale-covered reptile can swallow prey far bigger than its own head — and its paired organs sit one behind the other to fit a narrow body. What creature is it?
Working largely in isolation, this early-20th-century Indian mathematician solved problems thought unsolvable, though leading professionals first dismissed his work as too novel — who was he?
